title: Zalce: Maria's DNA is 30% completely different

tellings.quote: In the big bodies like Maria, the DNA show us that there were around 17 % known DNA, but there were 30 30% completely different.
One from chimpanzee, bonobo, one from another type of chimpanzee from Africa, and one type from the South Asian human primates.
tellings.difference: Puts the known share at about 70% and names the matching species (chimpanzee, bonobo, another African chimp, a South Asian primate), where the story gives around 17% known and 30% different.
tellings.link_reason: Zalce himself describing the DNA analysis of Maria: part of it matches known primates, the rest is unknown. This is the same analysis as the existing Zalce story.

as_told.title: Maria's DNA: 70% known with chimpanzee, bonobo and South Asian primate

plain: DNA tests on the large mummified bodies from Peru, such as one called Maria, showed about 17 percent known DNA but about 30 percent "completely different," according to Jose Zalce, who says he worked on these three-fingered bodies himself. In another passage he tells Michels, citing a man named David Ron Hell, that the known parts matched a chimpanzee, a bonobo, another African chimpanzee and a South Asian primate, which, if true, would mean the bodies are partly unlike anything known.
